messages.author: 496499cefe2ae056
messages.subject: stacked barcharts
parts:
Hi,

I have a dataframe with three columns. The first is a series of five
attributes of a product. The second is a series of ratings on each
attribute, three ratings per attribute such as "Too Much", "OK", "Too
Little". The third is the percent of consumers in a survey who rated
each attribute with that rating and the percents for an attribute sum to
100. There are 15 rows in the dataframe (5 attributes x 3 ratings). I
want to create a stacked barchart with five bars, each divided into
three segments, the length of the segments being the percents. The
bars, of course, should all be the same height. How can I do this? Any
advice is appreciated.

Thanks,

Walt

messages.subject: Re: stacked barcharts
parts:
You will want to use stat = "identity" to disable the default summarization of the data. See http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/geom_bar.html  for a number of examples. If you provide some sample data you would help out a lot.

Cheers,
Roman

messages.author: bfc2eb6b71169017
messages.subject: Re: stacked barcharts
parts:
Walt, I think this is what you're after. There's some more info on stacking and dodging here:  http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/geom_bar.html
You will probably want to modify your plot a bit. I suggest  https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/wiki/+opts()-List 

ggplot(wlt, aes(x = att, y = pct, fill = jar)) + geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack")

Cheers,
Roman
